svg.text: How four fragment-based notations tokenise the same molecule
Reference compound: 2-chloro-N-(4-methoxybenzyl)benzamide. Dashed red marks indicate cleaved bonds; colours match fragments to their tokens.
Atom-level tokenisation — 28 tokens, the baseline every method below compresses:
t-SMILES Wu et al., Nat. Commun. 2024
Fragment the graph, arrange the fragments as a full binary tree (FBT), then serialise by
breadth-first traversal. Two extra symbols carry the topology.
& = placeholder node (no real fragment) · ^ = fragment separator · joins are dummy atoms [n*] matched in pairs.
Topology lives in the tree, not in nested brackets — this shortens long-range grammatical dependencies.
full binary tree — breadth-first read-out gives the string above
fragSMILES Mastrolorito et al., Commun. Chem. 2025
Cleave all exocyclic single bonds, collapse the molecule to a reduced graph whose nodes are
canonical fragment SMILES, then write that graph as a string.
<i> tags name the connecting atom of a fragment, so each fragment is encoded identically in every context (no redundancy).
Chirality is written as an explicit R/S suffix, making it invariant to traversal order — unlike @/@@ in SMILES.
SAFE Noutahi et al., Digital Discovery 2024
Fragment (BRICS by default) and rewrite each fragment as a block; attachment points become
ring-closure digits and blocks are separated by dots.
The string stays a syntactically valid SMILES — any SMILES parser reads it, so no new tokeniser or decoder is required.
Block order is unconstrained, which makes scaffold decoration and linker design expressible as simple sequence in-filling.
SMILES Pair Encoding (SPE) Li & Fourches, J. Chem. Inf. Model. 2021
No chemical fragmentation at all: learn the most frequent adjacent-symbol merges from a corpus
(byte-pair encoding on atom-level SMILES tokens) and store them as a vocabulary.
Data-driven, not rule-driven: tokens are frequent substrings, so they need not be chemically meaningful.
Here Cl)cc1 merges the chlorine with a branch-close and two atoms of the other ring — a valid token spanning no single substructure.
